text.what: Under two hectares of Vosne-Romanée hillside, held by one owner, producing about 3,500 bottles a year. No other patch of ground in wine carries this much argument per square metre.
text.story: Louis François de Bourbon, prince de Conti, bought it in 1760 through an agent and kept the wine for himself; the name stuck. It survived phylloxera on ungrafted vines until 1945, when the harvest fell to about 2.5 hl/ha and 600 bottles, and the vineyard was pulled and replanted.

kin.as: Its sole owner, and the domaine named after it.
The other monopole down the same slope.
